```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Sun_2024_tacrolimus")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2024.1502097>
* Description: `r ui$description`

Sun 2024 develops a single population PK model, so this paper contributes one
model file. It comes from the same Second Xiangya Hospital group as
`Zhao_2024_tacrolimus`, which modelled the same drug pair in the first 15 days
after transplantation; Sun 2024 is a separate, prospective cohort of patients
at least one year post-transplant and a separately estimated model.

# Population

51 adult renal transplant recipients treated at The Second Xiangya Hospital of
Central South University, Changsha, China, enrolled prospectively between
April 2023 and September 2024. All were at least one year post-transplant, on
oral immediate-release tacrolimus (typically twice daily) with mycophenolate
mofetil and a glucocorticoid, and on concomitant oral voriconazole. Patients on
other immunosuppressants or on potent CYP450 inducers or inhibitors were
excluded.

Baseline characteristics (Sun 2024 Table 1): 37 male (72.55%) and 14 female;
median age 45 years (IQR 38-55); median weight 59.6 kg (IQR 51.1-67.2); median
tacrolimus concentration 5.80 ng/mL (IQR 4.20-8.65); median voriconazole
concentration 0.95 ug/mL (IQR 0.00-2.64); median red blood cell count 3.44 x
10^12/L (IQR 2.82-4.12); median platelet count 170 x 10^9/L (IQR 129-220);
median serum creatinine 172 umol/L (IQR 120-277).

281 whole-blood tacrolimus concentrations were collected with a sparse design:
patients were randomised to one of three sampling groups (0, 0.5 and 1 h; 2, 4
and 6 h; 8 h and 30 min before the next dose), with at least five
concentrations per patient.

The same information is available programmatically from `ui$population`.

# Source trace

Per-parameter origins are recorded as in-file comments beside each `ini()`
entry; they are collected here for review.

| Quantity | Value | Source location |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| Structural model: one compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | n/a | Section 2.3.2 and section 3.2; Table 2 row `1a_Add_Multiplicative` (lowest AIC among the one-compartment models) |
| Residual model: additive + multiplicative | n/a | Table 2 row `1a_Add_Multiplicative`; section 3.2 |
| `Ka` (fixed) | 3.09 1/h | Table 3 row `Ka (Fix)` (Stderr 0.00, CI 3.09-3.09); Table 4 |
| `V/F` | 1635.34 L | Table 3 row `V/F`; Table 4 bootstrap median 1626.24 (95% CI 1313.12-2013.20) |
| `CL/F` | 5.73 L/h | Table 3 row `CL/F`; Table 4 bootstrap median 5.74 (95% CI 4.65-7.07) |
| RBC exponent on CL/F | -1.34 | Table 3 row `dCldRBC`; Table 4 row `Theta RBC-CL` |
| PLT exponent on CL/F | 0.46 | Table 3 row `dCldPLT`; Table 4 row `Theta PLT-CL` |
| Voriconazole coefficient on CL/F | -0.12 | Table 3 row `dCldCvRc`; Table 4 row `Theta Cvrc-CL` |
| Voriconazole coefficient on V/F | -0.07 | Table 3 row `dVdCVRC`; Table 4 row `Theta Cvrc-V` |
| Covariate equations, centring constants 1.70 ug/mL, 3.49 x 10^12/L, 181.24 x 10^9/L | n/a | Section 3.2, equations for `V` and `Cl` |
| `omega^2` V | 0.091 | Table 4 row `omega 2 V` |
| `omega^2` CL | 0.039 | Table 4 row `omega 2 CL` |
| Proportional residual SD | 0.36 | Table 3 row `tvCMultStdev`; section 3.2 `CMultStdev = 0.36` |
| Additive residual SD | 0.04 ng/mL | Table 3 row `stdev0`; Table 4 row `sigma` |

The final-model equations printed in section 3.2 are

```
V  = 1635.34 * (1 + (Cvrc - 1.70) * (-0.07)) * exp(nV)
Cl = 5.73 * (RBC / 3.49)^(-1.34) * (PLT / 181.24)^(0.46)
          * (1 + (Cvrc - 1.70) * (-0.12)) * exp(nCL)
```

with `Cvrc` in ug/mL. The model takes voriconazole in the canonical ng/mL
column `CONC_VORI_NGML` and divides by 1000 before applying these equations.

# Covariate effects on the typical parameters

With the random effects zeroed, the solved `cl` and `vc` must equal the
section 3.2 equations evaluated by hand. This check has no random component.

```{r covariate-equations}
typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

covGrid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  cvrc = c(0, 0.95, 1.70, 2.64, 5),
  RBC = c(2.82, 3.49, 4.12),
  PLT = c(129, 181.24, 220)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

evCov <- covGrid |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, time = 0, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
    CONC_VORI_NGML = cvrc * 1000, RBC, PLT
  )

simCov <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, evCov, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl, vc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(covGrid, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    clPaper = 5.73 * (RBC / 3.49)^(-1.34) * (PLT / 181.24)^(0.46) *
      (1 + (cvrc - 1.70) * (-0.12)),
    vcPaper = 1635.34 * (1 + (cvrc - 1.70) * (-0.07))
  )

stopifnot(
  max(abs(simCov$cl / simCov$clPaper - 1)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(simCov$vc / simCov$vcPaper - 1)) < 1e-10
)

knitr::kable(
  simCov |>
    dplyr::filter(RBC == 3.49, PLT == 181.24) |>
    dplyr::select(cvrc, cl, vc) |>
    dplyr::mutate(clFold = cl / 5.73, vcFold = vc / 1635.34) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Voriconazole (ug/mL)" = cvrc,
      "CL/F (L/h)" = cl,
      "V/F (L)" = vc,
      "CL/F vs typical" = clFold,
      "V/F vs typical" = vcFold
    ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical CL/F and V/F against voriconazole concentration at RBC = 3.49 x 10^12/L and PLT = 181.24 x 10^9/L (section 3.2 equations)."
)
```

Across the observed interquartile range of voriconazole (0 to 2.64 ug/mL) the
typical CL/F falls from `r round(5.73 * (1 + 1.70 * 0.12), 2)` to
`r round(5.73 * (1 - (2.64 - 1.70) * 0.12), 2)` L/h, about a 26% reduction.
The red blood cell effect is the largest of the three over the cohort's
interquartile range: CL/F at RBC = 2.82 x 10^12/L is
`r round((2.82 / 4.12)^(-1.34), 2)`-fold that at 4.12 x 10^12/L. The platelet
effect over its interquartile range (129 to 220 x 10^9/L) is
`r round((220 / 129)^0.46, 2)`-fold.

```{r covariate-plot, echo = FALSE}
cvrcLine <- seq(0, 6, by = 0.1)
data.frame(
  cvrc = rep(cvrcLine, 2),
  parameter = rep(c("CL/F", "V/F"), each = length(cvrcLine)),
  fold = c(1 + (cvrcLine - 1.70) * (-0.12), 1 + (cvrcLine - 1.70) * (-0.07))
) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(cvrc, fold, colour = parameter)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 2.64, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Voriconazole concentration (ug/mL)",
    y = "Fold change vs typical value at 1.70 ug/mL",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Shaded: cohort interquartile range of voriconazole concentration (Table 1)."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

# Structural verification against the closed form

At steady state on a q12h schedule the one-compartment first-order-absorption
model has an exact closed form. A typical patient at the centring covariates
dosed 0.5 mg q12h is solved with `ss = 1` and compared against it. The
apparent half-life at these values is
`r round(log(2) * 1635.34 / 5.73)` h, so steady state takes weeks to reach
and the steady-state solve needs a larger step budget and tight tolerances.

```{r closedform}
kaRef <- 3.09
clRef <- 5.73
vcRef <- 1635.34
doseMg <- 0.5
tau <- 12
obsT <- seq(0, tau, by = 0.25)

evSs <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = 0, amt = doseMg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ss = 1L, ii = tau),
  data.frame(time = obsT, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ss = 0L, ii = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, CONC_VORI_NGML = 1700, RBC = 3.49, PLT = 181.24) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))

simSs <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  typ, evSs, returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
)

kelRef <- clRef / vcRef
closedSs <- 1000 * doseMg * kaRef / (vcRef * (kaRef - kelRef)) *
  (exp(-kelRef * simSs$time) / (1 - exp(-kelRef * tau)) -
     exp(-kaRef * simSs$time) / (1 - exp(-kaRef * tau)))

relDiff <- abs(simSs$Cc / closedSs - 1)
summary(relDiff)
stopifnot(max(relDiff) < 1e-5)
```

```{r closedform-plot, echo = FALSE}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  data.frame(time = simSs$time, solved = simSs$Cc, closed = closedSs),
  ggplot2::aes(time)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = solved, colour = "rxode2 solve"), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = ~ dplyr::filter(.x, time %% 1 == 0),
    ggplot2::aes(y = closed, colour = "closed form"), size = 1.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Tacrolimus, whole blood (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    title = "0.5 mg q12h at steady state, typical patient at the centring covariates"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

Sun 2024 does not tabulate the tacrolimus doses. At the cohort-median
voriconazole concentration (0.95 ug/mL) and the centring RBC and platelet
counts, the model's average steady-state concentration equals the observed
cohort median of 5.80 ng/mL at a dose of about
`r round(5.80 * 12 * 5.73 * (1 + (0.95 - 1.70) * (-0.12)) / 1000, 2)` mg q12h.
That is a low dose for tacrolimus, in line with the paper's remark that
clinicians gave patients on long-term tacrolimus smaller doses and with the
CYP3A inhibition by voriconazole. The 0.5 mg q12h regimen used throughout this
article is chosen on that basis; it is an illustration, not a dose from the
paper.

# Simulated cohort on the paper's sampling design

Three voriconazole levels spanning the cohort distribution (0, the median 0.95
and the upper quartile 2.64 ug/mL), 100 virtual patients each, dosed 0.5 mg
q12h to steady state. Red blood cell and platelet counts are drawn log-normally
to match the Table 1 medians and interquartile ranges. Observation times are
the union of the three sampling groups in section 2.3.1, with "30 min before
the next dose" taken as 11.5 h.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() for the base-R covariate draws, rxSetSeed() for the etas.
set.seed(20241502)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241502)
nPerArm <- 100L
arms <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Cvrc 0 ug/mL", "Cvrc 0.95 ug/mL", "Cvrc 2.64 ug/mL"),
  cvrc = c(0, 0.95, 2.64)
)

# log-normal SDs from the Table 1 IQRs: (log(Q3) - log(Q1)) / 1.349
subjects <- tidyr::expand_grid(arm = seq_len(nrow(arms)), k = seq_len(nPerArm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    treatment = arms$treatment[arm],
    cvrc = arms$cvrc[arm],
    RBC = 3.44 * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, (log(4.12) - log(2.82)) / 1.349)),
    PLT = 170 * exp(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, (log(220) - log(129)) / 1.349))
  )

sampleT <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 11.5, 12)
gridT <- sort(unique(c(sampleT, seq(0, 12, by = 0.25))))

evCohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  subjects |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = doseMg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ss = 1L, ii = tau),
  tidyr::expand_grid(subjects, time = gridT) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ss = 0L, ii = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CONC_VORI_NGML = cvrc * 1000) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, ss, ii, CONC_VORI_NGML, RBC, PLT) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

simCohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, evCohort, returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subjects, id, treatment), by = "id")

stopifnot(!anyNA(simCohort$Cc))
```

```{r cohort-plot, echo = FALSE}
simCohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(time, p50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = sampleT, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Tacrolimus, whole blood (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "0.5 mg q12h at steady state: median and 90% prediction interval",
    caption = "Dotted lines: sampling times of the three sampling groups (section 2.3.1)."
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()
```

The paper's Figure 3 VPC plots observed concentrations against an
independent-variable axis of up to 600 h of clinical time with clinician-titrated
doses that are not tabulated, so it cannot be regenerated without the dosing
records. The cohort above shows instead what the model predicts at the paper's
sampling times for a fixed regimen.

```{r cohort-sampling}
atSamples <- simCohort |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% sampleT[sampleT < 12]) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(sim),
    q25 = quantile(sim, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(sim, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  atSamples |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Arm" = treatment,
      "Median (ng/mL)" = median,
      "25th percentile" = q25,
      "75th percentile" = q75
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Simulated tacrolimus concentrations pooled over the eight sampling times, 0.5 mg q12h. Observed cohort (all doses pooled, Table 1): median 5.80 ng/mL, IQR 4.20-8.65."
)
```

At the median voriconazole level the simulated spread is close to the
observed Table 1 median and interquartile range. That agreement is not an
independent check of the model: the regimen was chosen above so that the
typical average concentration matches the observed median. What it does show
is that the published inter-individual variability, together with the RBC and
platelet spread, gives a concentration spread of the same width as the
observed one.

# PKNCA validation

Sun 2024 reports no non-compartmental analysis, so there is no published
Cmax / AUC table to compare against. PKNCA is used two ways.

First, as an internal identity on the typical patient: at steady state
`AUC(0-tau) = Dose / (CL/F)` exactly, so PKNCA's dosing-interval AUC at each
voriconazole level must recover the CL/F that the section 3.2 equation gives.

```{r pknca-typical}
evNcaTyp <- arms |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    id = id, treatment = treatment, cvrc = cvrc,
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      data.frame(time = 0, amt = doseMg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ss = 1L, ii = tau),
      data.frame(time = obsT, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ss = 0L, ii = 0)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CONC_VORI_NGML = cvrc * 1000, RBC = 3.49, PLT = 181.24) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

simNcaTyp <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  typ, dplyr::select(evNcaTyp, -treatment, -cvrc), returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(evNcaTyp, id, treatment, cvrc), by = "id")

concTyp <- simNcaTyp |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
doseTyp <- concTyp |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, dose_mg = doseMg)

ssIntervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)

ncaTyp <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(concTyp, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doseTyp, dose_mg ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = ssIntervals
  )
)

typCompare <- as.data.frame(ncaTyp) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(arms, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    clEquation = 5.73 * (1 + (cvrc - 1.70) * (-0.12)),
    aucExpected = 1000 * doseMg / clEquation,
    aucPctDiff = 100 * (auclast - aucExpected) / aucExpected
  )

knitr::kable(
  typCompare |>
    dplyr::select(treatment, cmax, tmax, cmin, auclast, aucExpected, aucPctDiff) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Arm" = treatment,
      "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
      "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
      "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
      "AUC0-12 NCA (ng/mL*h)" = auclast,
      "AUC0-12 Dose/CL" = aucExpected,
      "AUC % diff" = aucPctDiff
    ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical patient, 0.5 mg q12h at steady state: PKNCA dosing-interval AUC against Dose / (CL/F) from the section 3.2 equation."
)

stopifnot(
  # Linear-up/log-down trapezoids on a 0.25-h grid; measured error ~0.01%.
  max(abs(typCompare$aucPctDiff)) < 0.5,
  # Exposure rises with voriconazole, as the paper reports.
  all(diff(typCompare$auclast) > 0)
)
```

Second, as a per-arm summary of the simulated cohort, so the spread of
steady-state exposure across the three voriconazole levels can be read
directly. The PKNCA formula groups by arm.

```{r pknca-cohort}
concCohort <- simCohort |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
doseCohort <- concCohort |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, dose_mg = doseMg)

ncaCohort <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(concCohort, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doseCohort, dose_mg ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = ssIntervals
  )
)

cohortNca <- as.data.frame(ncaCohort) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    value = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median(PPORRES),
                    quantile(PPORRES, 0.25), quantile(PPORRES, 0.75)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)

knitr::kable(
  cohortNca |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Arm" = treatment,
      "AUC0-12 (ng/mL*h)" = auclast,
      "Cavg (ng/mL)" = cav,
      "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
      "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin
    ),
  caption = "Simulated cohort, 0.5 mg q12h at steady state: median [interquartile range] of individual NCA parameters by voriconazole level."
)

aucByArm <- as.data.frame(ncaCohort) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

foldHighLow <- aucByArm$auc[aucByArm$treatment == "Cvrc 2.64 ug/mL"] /
  aucByArm$auc[aucByArm$treatment == "Cvrc 0 ug/mL"]
foldTypical <- (1 + 1.70 * 0.12) / (1 - (2.64 - 1.70) * 0.12)
c(simulated = foldHighLow, typical = foldTypical)

stopifnot(
  # The arms are independent cohorts, so their median AUC ratio scatters around
  # the typical-value ratio (1.36). The per-subject CL/F spread (IIV plus the
  # RBC and PLT draws) is about 46% CV, giving a log-SE of the ratio of two
  # 100-subject medians near 0.08; the bound below is about 3 SE either side.
  foldHighLow > 1.05,
  foldHighLow < 1.75
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

1. **The voriconazole effect is linear and centred at 1.70 ug/mL, as printed.**
   The section 3.2 equations give `(1 + (Cvrc - 1.70) * theta)` on both CL/F
   and V/F. A linear covariate term can reach zero: CL/F does so at
   `r round(1.70 + 1 / 0.12, 2)` ug/mL and V/F at `r round(1.70 + 1 / 0.07, 2)`
   ug/mL. Those concentrations are within the assay's linear range
   (0.35-11.26 ug/mL) but far above the cohort's upper quartile of 2.64 ug/mL.
   The model file does not clamp the term; do not simulate it at voriconazole
   concentrations approaching 10 ug/mL. The centring value 1.70 is above the
   cohort median (0.95 ug/mL), and the RBC and PLT centring values (3.49 and
   181.24) likewise differ from the Table 1 medians (3.44 and 170); all three
   appear to be cohort means and are used exactly as printed.

2. **Power forms for RBC and platelets.** The MathML of the section 3.2
   `Cl` equation sets -1.34 and 0.46 as superscripts of `(RBC/3.49)` and
   `(PLT/181.24)`; the authors' manuscript supplement renders the same line
   with the superscripts flattened into multiplication. The exponent reading
   is used: the multiplicative reading would make CL/F negative.

3. **Residual error.** Phoenix NLME's additive-plus-multiplicative error model
   has variance `stdev0^2 + (CMultStdev * C)^2`, which is nlmixr2's default
   `add() + prop()` (combined2) form. `stdev0 = 0.04` is taken to be in
   ng/mL, the unit of the observations.

4. **`omega^2` values are variances.** Table 4 labels them `omega 2 V` and
   `omega 2 CL`; they are used directly. No covariance is reported, so the
   random effects are independent. The bootstrap median for `omega^2 CL`
   (0.063) differs from the final estimate (0.039); the final estimate is
   used.

5. **Whole blood.** Tacrolimus was measured with the ARCHITECT tacrolimus
   chemiluminescent immunoassay, a whole-blood method (section 2.3.1); the
   paper does not use the word "whole blood" itself.

6. **Doses and the VPC.** Tacrolimus and voriconazole doses were titrated by
   clinicians and are not tabulated, so Figure 3 (VPC) and Figure 2 (goodness
   of fit) cannot be regenerated. The 0.5 mg q12h regimen used here is chosen
   from the back-calculation above and is not from the paper.

7. **Time-varying covariates.** The paper does not say whether RBC, platelet
   count and voriconazole concentration were applied per sample or as
   baselines. Voriconazole was measured alongside tacrolimus and is most
   naturally time-varying; the model accepts all three as time-varying columns.

## Errata in the source

* **Male count.** Section 3.1 says "comprising 38 males"; Table 1 gives 37
  male (72.55%) and 14 female, which sums to 51 and is used here.
* **Table 3 confidence intervals for V/F and CL/F are on a different scale
  from the estimates** (V/F 1635.34 L with CI 1.30-1.97; CL/F 5.73 L/h with CI
  0.005-0.007), consistent with Phoenix having estimated them in thousands of
  litres. The Table 4 bootstrap intervals (1313.12-2013.20 L and 4.65-7.07 L/h)
  are on the reported scale and corroborate the point estimates.
* **Table 4 bootstrap CI for `Theta Cvrc-CL`** is printed as -0.20 to -0.38,
  which does not bracket the median of -0.12; -0.038 is presumably intended.
  The final estimate -0.12 is unaffected.
* **Voriconazole units in the Discussion.** The Discussion quotes the median
  voriconazole concentration as "0.95 [0.00, 2.64] ng/mL"; Table 1 and the
  assay description give ug/mL, which is used.
* **Abstract wording.** The Abstract calls CL the "volume of clearance rate"
  and omits the voriconazole effect on V/F; the Table 3 results and section
  3.2 equations are followed.
